topic: How the subconscious mind drives us on a daily basis
research_question: How does the subconscious mind influence daily human behavior, decision-making, habit formation, emotional responses, perception, and social interaction — and what mechanisms (neural, psychological, philosophical, and spiritual) explain this influence?

indic_traditions.scope: Indian philosophical and psychological traditions on subconscious/unconscious processes — Vedantic chitta/vāsanā/saṃskāra theory, Yogic citta-vṛtti-nirodha, Buddhist ālaya-vijñāna (store consciousness) and manas, Tantric conceptions of subliminal impulses, Abhinavagupta's consciousness theory, and modern Indian thinkers (Aurobindo's subliminal, Krishnamurti's unconscious).
known_sources: Yoga Sūtras of Patañjali — vāsanā, saṃskāra, kliṣṭa/akliṣṭa vṛttis
The Bhagavad Gītā — śraddhā, triguṇa-driven behavior
Vasubandhu — Triṃśikā (store consciousness, manas)
Śaṅkara — Vivekacūḍāmaṇi on avidyā and adhyāsa
Abhinavagupta — Tantrāloka (prakāśa-vimarśa, unconscious impulses)
Sri Aurobindo — The Life Divine, The Synthesis of Yoga (subconscious, subliminal, superconscious)
J. Krishnamurti — Commentaries on Living (the observer and the observed)
Sarvapalli Radhakrishnan — Indian Philosophy (on unconscious in Vedanta)
indic_traditions.special_instructions: Focus on practical daily-life mechanisms (how vāsanā patterns drive choices, how saṃskāra triggers emotional reactions). Include the Buddhist 'store consciousness' as it directly parallels modern unconscious memory systems. Krishnamurti is a living teacher per boundary rules — include him fully.

western_philosophy.scope: Western philosophical and psychological traditions on unconscious drives — Freudian dynamic unconscious (repression, parapraxes, dream-work), Jungian collective unconscious & archetypes, Schopenhauer's Will, Nietzsche's drives, phenomenological approaches (Husserl's passive synthesis, Merleau-Ponty's habitual body), and the cognitive unconscious (Bargh, Kahneman System 1).
known_sources: Sigmund Freud — The Interpretation of Dreams, The Psychopathology of Everyday Life, The Ego and the Id
Carl Jung — The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious, Man and His Symbols
Arthur Schopenhauer — The World as Will and Representation (Book 2 & 4)
Friedrich Nietzsche — Beyond Good and Evil (on drives), The Gay Science
Maurice Merleau-Ponty — Phenomenology of Perception (habit body, pre-reflective)
Edmund Husserl — Cartesian Meditations (passive genesis)
John Bargh — Before You Know It: The Unconscious Reasons We Do What We Do
Daniel Kahneman — Thinking, Fast and Slow (System 1 / System 2)
western_philosophy.special_instructions: Cover the full arc from 19th-century depth psychology through 21st-century cognitive unconscious. Distinguish the psychoanalytic unconscious (repressed content) from the cognitive unconscious (non-conscious processing).

ancient_civilizations.scope: Ancient and pre-modern perspectives on hidden psychic drives — Platonic tripartite soul (chariot allegory), Aristotelian phantasia, Neoplatonic emanation, Gnostic inner conflict, Hermetic mental laws (The Kybalion), Egyptian ba/ka/akh psychology, and Sufi psychology of nafs (lower self), qalb (heart), rūḥ (spirit).
known_sources: Plato — Phaedrus (chariot allegory), Republic (tripartite soul: logos, thymos, epithymia)
Plotinus — Enneads (on the unconscious depths of the soul, Intellect's pre-thinking)
Aristotle — De Anima (phantasia, orexis — desire and movement)
Al-Ghazālī — The Alchemy of Happiness (nafs, heart, spirit, intellect)
Ibn 'Arabī — Fuṣūṣ al-Ḥikam (levels of being, the unknown self)
Rūmī — Masnavi-ye Ma'navi (the subconscious self, the reed flute's yearning)
Hermetic texts — The Kybalion (the Seven Hermetic Principles, mentalism, correspondence)
Egyptian Book of the Dead — ba, ka, akh, sheut (shadow-self)
ancient_civilizations.special_instructions: Focus on how each tradition conceptualized the 'hidden driver' of daily behavior — the parts of the psyche not under conscious control. Sufi nafs doctrine is particularly important as a detailed model of subconscious motivation.

contemporary_scholarship.scope: Modern interdisciplinary research on unconscious cognition — automaticity and priming (Bargh, Chartrand), adaptive unconscious (Wilson), behavioral economics and implicit attitudes (Kahneman, Tversky), predictive processing theories (Friston, Seth, Clark), emotion construction (Barrett), and social cognitive neuroscience of non-conscious behavior.
known_sources: John Bargh & Tanya Chartrand — The Unbearable Automaticity of Being (1999)
Timothy D. Wilson — Strangers to Ourselves: Discovering the Adaptive Unconscious
Daniel Kahneman — Thinking, Fast and Slow
Ap Dijksterhuis — The Unconscious: New Paradigms
Lisa Feldman Barrett — How Emotions Are Made: The Secret Life of the Brain
Anil Seth — Being You: A New Science of Consciousness
Andy Clark — Surfing Uncertainty: Prediction, Action, and the Embodied Mind
Karl Friston — The free-energy principle: a unified brain theory
John-Dylan Haynes — Brain reading and decoding unconscious thought
Tali Sharot — The Influential Mind (implicit biases and daily decisions)
contemporary_scholarship.special_instructions: Prioritize experimental and empirical findings that directly demonstrate subconscious influence on daily life — priming effects, implicit bias, automatic goal pursuit, non-conscious emotional processing. Bridge predictive processing with everyday experience.

science_technology.scope: Neuroscientific and computational perspectives on subliminal mental processes — neural correlates of unconscious processing (visual masking, blindsight), implicit vs. explicit memory systems (hippocampus vs. basal ganglia), habit formation neurocircuitry (cortico-striatal loops), predictive coding in the brain, the global neuronal workspace, AI models of implicit knowledge (deep learning's 'black box' as analog for subconscious), and neuromodulation of unconscious drives (dopamine, serotonin, norepinephrine).
known_sources: Stanislas Dehaene — Consciousness and the Brain: Deciphering How the Brain Codes Our Thoughts
Michael Gazzaniga — The Mind's Past (the interpreter module)
Ann Graybiel — Habits, rituals, and the evaluative brain (Annual Review of Neuroscience, 2008)
Wolfram Schultz — Dopamine reward prediction error coding
Bernard Baars — Global Workspace Theory of consciousness
Karl Friston — Active inference and learning (Neuroscience & Biobehavioral Reviews)
Anthony Damasio — The Feeling of What Happens: Body and Emotion in the Making of Consciousness
Chris Frith — Making up the Mind: How the Brain Creates Our Mental World
Daniel Dennett — Consciousness Explained (multiple drafts model)
David Marr — Vision (computational levels of analysis)
science_technology.special_instructions: Focus on neural mechanisms that operate below conscious awareness — the 'habit loop' in the basal ganglia, dopamine prediction error (how reward prediction runs subconsciously before any conscious feeling), the interpreter module (left-hemisphere confabulation of unconscious drives), and blindsight/neglect as evidence of non-conscious perception. Draw parallels between deep neural networks and the brain's non-conscious feature extraction.
